full_judgment: 2. On 14.7.81 pre-emptor respondents 1-3 Mohammad Islam, Kala Mia and Feroza Khatun of village Tetia, P.S. Cox's Bazar filed an application stating that Jyoti Prisad Rakshit and Tarun Tapan Rakshit (sons of late Barada Prasad Rakshit) of village Jayara, P.S. Chand Naish, Patiya, Chittagong sold 7.44. acre of Nal land out of 19.90 acre of land in R.S. plot Nos. 284, 299, 300, 2509, 2512, 2513, 2514, 2525, 2527, 307, 308, 2532, 282, 295, 296, 301, 302, 2517, 2.28, 286, 290, 2516, 2020, 2509, 2506, 281, 287, 280, 244, 287, 2544, 2507, 4167,  4171, 4172, 2521, 2523, 2527, 2529, 2530, 2531, 2532, 2540, 2546, 2548, 2555, 2556, 613, 615, 616, 619, 621, 622 and 625 of R.S. Khatian No. 136 (M.R.R. Khatian No. 191) having a Jama of Taka 75.25 of Mouza Tetiai P.S. Cox's Bazar to appellant O.Ps. 1-5 Sultan Ahmed, Syed Nur, Gura Mia, Badar Alain and Sarnuda Khatun of village Tetia, P.S. Cox's Bazar for Taka 1,00 000/- by a deed of sale (Ext. 1) executed and registered on 27.4.79 in the Chittagong Sadar Sub-Registrar's Office. Late Barada Prasad Rakshit, father of vendors Jyoti Prasad and Tarun Tapan had purchased the case land in 1941, Pre-emptee respondents 1-3 and other respondents 4-67 are co-sharers in the holding by inheritance and purchase. Transferors Jyoti Prasad and Tarun Tapan transferred the land in question without the knowledge of the pre-emptee respondents. and without serving any notice upon them. Appellant pre-emptee 1-4 and P.W. 2 Ula Mia used to cultivate the case land for 10/15 years as bargadars under Barada Prasad Rakshit and after latter's death under the vendors who are the heirs of Barada Prasad Rakshit. Pre-emptee appellants 1-5 are strangers to case land. P.W.2 Ula Mia used to cultivate three kanis of case land as bargadar. When as usual P.W.2 Ula Mia also wanted to cultivate the case land, pre-emptee appellants 1.4 . did not allow him to cultivate the case land stating that they had themselves purhased the same. On 1st Ashar 1388 B.S. corresponding to 16.6.81 A.D. the pre-emptor Respondents 1-3 came to know from P.W.2 Ula Mia for the first time that the pre-emptee appellants had purchased the case land. Pre-emptor respondent No. 1 Mohammad Islam then tried to find out if any such kabala had been registered at Cox's Bazar Sub-Registrar's Office or at Patiya Sub-Registrar's Office. Failing to get any trace of any such kabala there he went to Chittagong. Sub-Registrar's Office and succeeded in obtaining a certified copy of the kabala on 24.6.81, To keep the sale secret the pre-emptees registered the kabala at Sadar, Chittagong. The pre-emptor respondents 1-3 thus coming to know about the transfer for the first time instituted the present case on 14.7.81 praying for pre-emption depositing the consideration money of Taka 1,00,000/, with compensation of Taka 10,000/- Pre-emptors are agriculturists. It was also asserted in the petition by the pre-emptors that if they are allowed to pre-empt the case land, the total quantity of Land after adding the case laud to the land held by them and their families shall not exceed the maximum ceiling of land allowable under the law (section 90 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with P.O. No: 98 of 1972).
